sodium-volt.options.volt_guard_enabled.t: Protects frame stability by enforcing configurable render-work budgets when worlds, servers, or other mods create excessive visual workloads.
sodium-volt.options.adaptive_workload_co: Adjusts how aggressively Volt Guard applies its render budgets when sustained frame times fall below the target frame rate.
sodium-volt.options.prioritize_visible_e: Prioritizes nearby, on-screen visual effects before distant or off-screen decorative work when a render budget is exhausted.
sodium-volt.options.preserve_gameplay_cr: Reserves render capacity for important combat, interaction, and status effects before limiting decorative effects.
sodium-volt.options.show_protection_noti: Shows a notification when Volt Guard substantially limits a visual workload. This does not affect normal gameplay packets.
sodium-volt.options.target_fps.tooltip: Sets the frame-rate target used by Adaptive Workload Control. Higher targets cause Volt Guard to limit expensive visual work sooner.
sodium-volt.options.particle_render_budg: Sets the maximum particle workload Volt Guard may prioritize during a frame. Lower values can improve stability during particle spam but may hide more decorative particles.
sodium-volt.options.block_entity_render_: Sets the maximum block-entity workload Volt Guard may prioritize during a frame. Lower values can improve performance in dense builds but may defer distant block entities.
sodium-volt.options.display_entity_rende: Sets the maximum display-entity workload Volt Guard may prioritize during a frame. Lower values can protect against display spam but may defer distant displays.
sodium-volt.notification.protection_acti: Volt Guard stabilized this frame by deferring %s visual effects.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.enabled.to: Enables bounded local performance sampling. No server address, account, path, packet, or gameplay data is recorded or transmitted.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.show_overl: Shows the latest Inspector snapshot in a compact translucent HUD panel. Disabling it hides the panel while leaving enabled metric samplers available.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.frame_time: Measures a bounded frame window and reports average, median, p95, p99, and p99.5 frame times at the selected refresh interval.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.chunk_acti: Shows Sodium's visible chunk count, terrain completion state, builder queue/thread activity, and whether its transfer queue is reporting activity. It does not claim an exact upload count.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.scene_comp: Counts visible extracted entities, block entities, and display entities before Volt Guard applies its optional render budgets.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.particle_b: Samples active client particle objects only at refresh time and shows the five most common implementation-class labels.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.animated_t: Counts currently active atlas animation-state objects, such as animated block, item, and particle textures.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.gc_monitor: Shows JVM-reported garbage-collection count and collection-time changes. Collection time is not an exact stop-the-world pause measurement.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.bottleneck: Conservatively estimates CPU-bound, GPU-bound, mixed, or unclear pressure using Minecraft's GPU-utilization sample and high frame-time percentiles.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.renderer_d: Shows the active OpenGL or Vulkan backend plus sanitized GPU vendor, renderer, and driver strings supplied by Minecraft's render device.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.reload_tim: Measures asynchronous resource-pack reload completion time and whether the most recently observed reload succeeded, without blocking the game.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.recommenda: Shows at most three deterministic suggestions based on sustained local metrics. Suggestions are indicators, not definitive diagnoses.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.refresh_in: Controls how often expensive metrics and the displayed snapshot are refreshed. Frame sampling remains allocation-free between refreshes.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.sample_win: Sets the maximum number of recent valid frame intervals used for statistics. The minimum provides enough samples for a meaningful p99.5 estimate.
sodium-volt.options.inspector.spike_thre: Sets the high-frame-time threshold used by the bottleneck estimate and smart recommendations.
Dynamically adjusts selected client-only graphics settings from sustained frame-time pressure. It never changes VSync, the framerate cap, simulation distance, game rules, networking, or world state.
Selects the controller's starting quality and recovery policy. Every profile obeys the live Minecraft framerate cap and VSync refresh ceiling.

Keeps the player's captured graphics baseline, bounded by the configured maximum render distance, respects the live framerate cap and VSync, and makes ordered reversible reductions only after sustained target pressure.

Starts at the highest safely live-adjustable graphics values within the render-distance ceiling, then reduces them only under sustained target pressure. Reload-bound mipmap and texture-filter settings are deliberately left unchanged.

Starts at the lowest selected graphics tiers for maximum FPS. With a finite target it may recover only three visual-effect tiers, keeping particles, entity distance, and render distance performance-biased.
sodium-volt.options.performance.target_f: Sets the desired sustained frame rate. Max Framerate uses the current Minecraft cap or VSync refresh ceiling; when both are unlimited, the selected profile holds its intended baseline instead of guessing an unreachable target.
sodium-volt.options.performance.render_d: Allows bounded render-distance changes between the configured minimum and maximum after cheaper particle and entity-distance reductions are exhausted.
sodium-volt.options.performance.entity_d: Allows the controller to reduce client entity draw distance before reducing render distance when sustained frame times miss the target.
sodium-volt.options.performance.particle: Allows deterministic All, Decreased, and Minimal particle-quality tiers. This is the controller's first downshift and complements rather than duplicates Volt Guard's render-work budgets.
sodium-volt.options.performance.visual_e: Allows bounded changes to safely live-adjustable visual options such as clouds, ambient occlusion, shadows, biome blending, leaves, transparency, vignette, weather range, and chunk-section fade.
sodium-volt.options.performance.animatio: Under severe sustained pressure, updates block-world and particle atlas animations every other client tick. Item, GUI, and all other atlases are exempt; world simulation is never slowed. This opt-in experimental throttle restores immediately when pressure or the toggle clears.
sodium-volt.options.performance.restore_: Restores the exact graphics values captured when the controller activated or changed profile. Clean client shutdown also restores and saves them once.
sodium-volt.options.performance.notifica: Shows rate-limited HUD messages for profile activation, quality downshifts, and recoveries. Disabling this has no effect on control behavior.
sodium-volt.options.performance.min_rend: Sets the lowest render distance the controller may use. The saved minimum and maximum are cross-validated so the minimum never exceeds the maximum.
sodium-volt.options.performance.max_rend: Sets the highest render distance Max Quality may request and the ceiling used by other profiles. Server-provided effective-distance limits still apply.
sodium-volt.options.performance.adjustme: Controls how often the bounded frame window is evaluated. Shorter intervals react faster; pressure still requires consecutive confirmations.
sodium-volt.options.performance.recovery: Requires sustained headroom for this long after pressure before one quality tier can recover, reducing visible oscillation.
sodium-volt.options.performance.fps_tole: Creates a hysteresis band around the effective target. The controller downshifts below target minus tolerance and recovers above target plus tolerance.
sodium-volt.options.performance.sample_w: Sets the fixed-size recent frame window used for p95 evaluation. Frame sampling performs no per-frame allocations and ignores pauses, menus, loading overlays, and absent worlds.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.ena: Enables bounded client-side particle render scheduling and optional distance-aware simulation cadence. Render scans stop at 32,768 particles per frame and fail open beyond that cap. It never changes packets, server state, world data, Sodium settings, or particle spawning.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.pri: Reserves per-type and ambient-cell capacity for quad particles inside Minecraft's current camera frustum. It does not bypass Minecraft's own frustum culling.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.ski: Skips extraction of non-critical particles whose center is fully behind the camera. Their client simulation and lifetime continue normally.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.dis: Runs distant non-critical particle-specific tick logic less often while advancing base age every client tick, freezing skipped-tick interpolation, and preserving the vanilla lifetime boundary. Near and critical particles remain full-rate.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.pre: Gives directly classified combat, interaction, status, and pickup particle implementations full-rate simulation and first render capacity within a hard reserve. Excess critical particles rejoin normal bounded scheduling.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.coa: Renders only a bounded number of equivalent ambient particle implementations per fixed 4-block cell. This is render-only: particle objects, simulation, age, and server behavior are unchanged.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.per: Limits extraction per concrete particle implementation each frame. Capacity is deterministic and bounded; unsupported or saturated scheduler tables fail open.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.ins: Show Scheduler Stats in Volt Inspector
Adds bounded session counters and at most three sanitized implementation labels to the Volt Inspector HUD. Stats distinguish render suppression from age-only simulation skips.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.ful: Keeps particle-specific tick logic at full rate within this distance from the local player. Increasing it preserves more distant motion at a higher CPU cost.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.far: Runs distant non-critical particle-specific logic once per selected number of client ticks. Base age still advances every tick, so higher values reduce CPU work without extending particle lifetime.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.per: Sets the maximum particles extracted per concrete implementation each frame after the bounded critical reserve. Lower values reduce particle rendering work during single-type spam.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.amb: Sets how many equivalent ambient particles may render in each fixed 4-block cell per frame. Lower values reduce dense smoke, ash, leaf, snow, and suspended-particle overdraw.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vaps.cri: Sets the hard per-frame render reserve and per-tick distant full-rate simulation reserve for directly classified critical particles. Excess particles rejoin normal bounded scheduling so critical-tagged spam cannot bypass all limits.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.ena: Enables bounded client-render extraction cadence and final render-state budgets for block entities. It never changes block-entity simulation, packets, NBT, world data, or Sodium settings. The feature fails open if its bounded scheduler cannot safely classify work.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.pri: Plans the bounded final render list in this order: targeted or recently used, breaking, near, medium, then far. Turning this off keeps target/recent protection but otherwise follows extraction order.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.rec: Temporarily keeps the last locally used block entity fresh and gives it protected render capacity. The current crosshair target is always protected while this feature is enabled.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.dis: Extracts near block-entity render states every frame while medium and far states can reuse a validated cached state until their selected update interval. This changes rendering cadence only, never block-entity ticks.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.cac: Cache Medium and Far Render States

Keeps a fixed-capacity identity-validated cache so eligible medium and far vanilla block entities can skip some renderer state-extraction calls. Removed, replaced, changed-state, expired, world-switched, and resource-reloaded entries are rejected or cleared.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.per: Applies a bounded per-frame quota to each block-entity type as well as the global quota, preventing one type from consuming the complete render-state budget. Saturated scheduler tables fail open.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.cul: Skips vanilla client render-state extraction beyond the configured far distance, except for the current target, the recent interaction, and active breaking overlays. Modded renderers remain exempt; the block entity continues to exist, tick, and synchronize normally.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.inc: Opts modded block entities into distance-aware extraction cadence and render-state caching. Off by default for compatibility: modded block entities otherwise extract fresh, but still participate in the generic final global and per-type render budgets.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.ins: Show Budgeting Stats in Volt Inspector
Shows bounded session counters, cache occupancy, and at most three sanitized block-entity type identifiers in Volt Inspector. No world, account, server, path, packet, or NBT data is recorded.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.nea: Keeps eligible block-entity renderer state extraction fresh inside this distance. Increasing it preserves the most immediate animation detail at a higher CPU cost.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.med: Defines where the medium render-state cadence ends and the farther cadence begins. Saved near, medium, and far distances are cross-normalized in ascending order.
Refreshes eligible cached medium-distance render states at most once per selected number of client world ticks. Cache misses, targets, interactions, and breaking overlays always extract fresh.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.far: Refreshes eligible cached far render states at most once per selected number of client world ticks. Higher values reduce renderer extraction CPU cost but can make distant visual-only animations update less often.
Sets the optional far-cull boundary and the maximum configured distance boundary. Culling remains disabled unless Cull Beyond Far Distance is explicitly enabled.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.glo: Sets the normal number of block-entity render states retained per frame before Volt Guard processes the survivors. A tiny bounded target/recent reserve can exceed this quota; breaking overlays have a bounded reserve within it.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.per: Sets the normal maximum retained render states for each block-entity type per frame. Lower values reduce single-type renderer spam; target/recent protection is separately hard-bounded.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.gra: Sets how long the most recently used block position receives fresh extraction and protected render capacity. Only one bounded client-side position is retained and it is cleared on world changes.
sodium-volt.options.performance.berp.cac: Sets the fixed maximum cached render-state entries. Entries use bounded lookup probes, round-robin eviction, identity and block-state validation, and time-based expiry; lowering this value releases excess references.
sodium-volt.options.performance.att.enab: Enables bounded client-only scheduling for animated atlas states. It can pause unseen animations and reduce distant update cadence without changing texture files, resource packs, networking, world ticks, Sodium settings, or animation data on disk. Mapping or scheduler uncertainty fails open to Minecraft's normal animation tick.
sodium-volt.options.performance.att.paus: Pauses eligible block and particle animation-state ticks when neither Sodium's latest visible chunk scan nor another active client use references the sprite. The fixed initialization warmup, interface use, exemptions, and unknown activity remain full speed.
sodium-volt.options.performance.att.dist: Uses the nearest visible Sodium render-section distance to update far block animations less often. Near sprites, unknown or interface-only activity, exemptions, and newly resumed sprites remain full speed.
sodium-volt.options.performance.att.inte: Keeps item, GUI, font, painting, and other non-block/non-particle atlases at Minecraft's normal cadence. While a screen or overlay is open, active uses from block and particle atlases are also protected conservatively.
sodium-volt.options.performance.att.crit: Protects an exact built-in list of water, lava, fire, portal, clock, compass, and recovery-compass sprite identifiers. Matching is exact; no broad path or substring rules are used.
sodium-volt.options.performance.att.hono: Honors up to 64 validated user IDs from att_user_exempt_textures and up to 64 pack IDs loaded from assets/<namespace>/sodium_volt/animated_texture_exemptions.json. Files are capped at 16 KiB each, 64 files and 128 KiB total. Only 64 exempt animation ticks per atlas cycle may bypass the normal budget; excess entries rejoin bounded scheduling.
sodium-volt.options.performance.att.imme: Ticks a newly visible eligible sprite immediately instead of waiting for its distant cadence phase. It never performs multiple catch-up ticks or rewrites animation time.
sodium-volt.options.performance.att.insp: Show ATT Stats in Volt Inspector

Shows bounded saturating counters for normal ticks, invisible pauses, cadence skips, budget skips, exemptions, visibility scan caps, and mapping fail-open events. It records no paths, servers, accounts, packets, or texture contents.
sodium-volt.options.performance.att.full: Keeps visible eligible block animations at normal cadence within this nearest render-section distance. Increasing it preserves more nearby motion at a higher client CPU and upload cost.
sodium-volt.options.performance.att.dist: Ticks visible eligible animations beyond the full-speed distance once per selected number of client ticks. Severe APC animation pressure may also apply an every-other-tick cadence to otherwise eligible near world textures, while protected interface and exempt sprites remain full speed.
sodium-volt.options.performance.att.unse: Fully Paused (the default) stops eligible animations as soon as they become unseen after the fixed warmup. A nonzero compatibility value keeps a recently visible sprite ticking for that many client ticks before pausing it.
sodium-volt.options.performance.att.per_: Sets the normal animation ticks allowed per eligible atlas cycle; the cross-atlas normal limit is twice this value per client tick. A separate hard reserve of 64 exact exemptions per atlas sits outside the normal budget. Mapping and raw visibility work have independent fixed caps; overflow remains fail-open.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.ena: Tracks a bounded estimate of Minecraft and Sodium GPU texture, mip, framebuffer attachment, chunk-buffer, uniform, shader, and driver-headroom demand. It can warn and gradually cap client render distance before heavy swapping or driver instability. This is an estimate, never exact VRAM usage; it changes no networking, world simulation, texture files, resource packs, or mipmap setting.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.aut: Uses a cached native dedicated-memory total only when the active render backend exposes one reliably; otherwise uses a deliberately conservative, hard-capped fraction of physical memory rather than assuming a discrete GPU's capacity. Unified-memory systems share RAM with the CPU and use a separate capped fraction, so every automatic budget remains an estimate. Unknown metrics fail open.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.saf: Under sustained estimated pressure, gradually lowers only the client render-distance cap so Sodium can unload chunk meshes. Critical pressure steps faster but remains cooldown-bounded. Turning this off removes its cap immediately and restores only an owned value when recovery restoration is enabled. It never changes simulation distance, packets, mipmaps, textures, shaders, or resource files.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.spi: Requests an early pressure evaluation after one successfully tracked GPU allocation reaches the configured estimate. It does not block, cancel, resize, or delete that allocation; sustained and cooldown rules still bound quality changes.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.res: After estimated pressure remains safely below hysteresis for the recovery delay, raises Sodium Volt's owned render-distance cap one step at a time. Turning this off releases the hidden cap after recovery but leaves the visible reduced value unchanged. It never raises the user's or APC's lower setting and restores only values the engine still owns.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.war: Shows a rate-limited client overlay warning only in a valid loaded world when the estimated pressure state changes. Messages contain no server, account, path, resource identifier, or packet data.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.hea: Adds configurable percentage headroom and a fixed reserve for driver allocations, shader resources, backend metadata, temporary uploads, and other demand the low-level tracker cannot attribute precisely. Higher values protect earlier but may reduce render distance sooner.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.ins: Show VRAM Estimate in Volt Inspector

Shows bounded saturating estimates for usage, budget, pressure state, textures, buffers, render targets, peak, spikes, actions, source, and current safe cap. No raw GPU labels, texture IDs, paths, worlds, servers, or accounts are retained.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.man: Sets the comparison budget used when automatic detection is disabled. Choose a conservative amount available to Minecraft, not necessarily the advertised physical total. The tracker remains an estimate on every vendor and backend.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.pro: Starts sustained-pressure protection when the estimated demand reaches this percentage of the selected budget. Lower values act earlier and can reduce chunk view distance more often.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.cri: Marks estimated pressure critical and permits a faster bounded render-distance reduction. Saved values are normalized to remain at least five percentage points above the protection threshold.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.hea: Adds this percentage of tracked texture, mip, framebuffer, chunk-buffer, and other GPU allocations as untracked driver/shader safety demand. This is deliberately conservative and not a measurement.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.fix: Adds a fixed estimate for shader programs, driver caches, temporary resource-reload uploads, framebuffer transitions, and backend resources not represented by live texture/buffer objects.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.min: Sets the lowest client render-distance cap VRAM protection may own. Lower values release more Sodium chunk meshes under pressure but reduce visible terrain. Simulation distance and server behavior are untouched.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.sam: Samples constant-time tracker counters at this interval on the client thread. Longer intervals reduce already tiny controller overhead but react more slowly; allocation spikes can request an earlier bounded sample.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.sus: Requires this many consecutive protection or critical samples before changing the safe profile. Higher values reject short resource-reload peaks more strongly but delay protection.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.ste: Sets the minimum time between owned render-distance cap changes. Critical pressure may reduce by two chunks per permitted step; normal protection and recovery use one.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.rec: Requires estimated demand to remain below the hysteresis recovery boundary for this duration before restoring one owned cap step. Texture mip levels are never changed automatically because reloads can create their own allocation spikes.
sodium-volt.options.performance.vram.spi: Sets the single-allocation estimate that requests an early pressure evaluation. This covers large texture/mipmap, framebuffer, shader/uniform, and Sodium chunk-arena buffer allocations without retaining their labels or identifiers.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.enabled.to: Applies transient frame-rate caps while Minecraft is minimized, unfocused, or running on a known battery state. Caps compose with Minecraft's own limiter and VSync, never raise FPS, never rewrite or save vanilla video options, and disappear immediately when no configured condition applies.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.minimized_: Sets the maximum frame rate requested immediately when the real game window is minimized or iconified. Minecraft's own iconified limit, VSync, or a lower Max Framerate may remain stricter, so this cap never raises an existing limit.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.throttle_m: Applies Target FPS immediately when Minecraft reports its window as minimized or iconified. This is separate from ordinary focus loss and does not wait for the background delay.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.throttle_u: Applies the unfocused cap after Minecraft remains non-minimized and unfocused for the configured delay. Refocusing releases this cap immediately without changing Max Framerate or VSync.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.unfocused_: Sets the maximum frame rate while the non-minimized game window remains unfocused after the activation delay. Lower user, VSync, battery, or Minecraft limits still win.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.background: Waits this many continuous seconds before applying only the non-minimized unfocused cap. Minimized throttling remains immediate; focus restoration is immediate, and clock rollback restarts the delay safely.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.battery_mo: Polls local power state on one daemon worker and applies a transient cap only when battery and charge state are known. Missing, ambiguous, or failed power data fails open without affecting minimized or unfocused throttling.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.battery_ta: Sets the maximum frame rate when a known battery is discharging, or while charging when charging bypass is disabled. Background and lower vanilla limits compose by taking the minimum.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.bypass_cha: Releases both normal and low-battery caps when local power data reliably reports charging or external power. Unknown charging state always fails open; minimized and unfocused caps remain independent.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.low_batter: Uses the stricter low-battery target when a known retained percentage reaches the configured threshold. No battery name, serial number, device path, account, network, or telemetry data is retained or transmitted.
Sets the inclusive known battery percentage at which the low-battery frame cap becomes eligible. Unknown percentage or charge state fails open instead of limiting foreground performance.
Sets the maximum frame rate at or below the known low-battery threshold. The effective limiter is still the minimum of this, background, vanilla, and VSync constraints.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.power_poll: Sets how often a single bounded cached local battery query may be scheduled off the render thread. Longer intervals reduce tiny system-query overhead but make plug and percentage changes update more slowly.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.notificati: Shows strictly rate-limited transition messages only inside a loaded world with no menu or overlay open. It does not repeat every frame or expose device, server, account, path, or battery identifiers.
sodium-volt.options.smart_fps.inspector_: Show Smart FPS Stats in Volt Inspector

Adds a bounded Smart FPS status summary with active reasons, effective cap, window focus/minimized state, and only known charge state and percentage. Unknown data is labeled unknown; no device identifiers are retained.
sodium-volt.notification.vram.protection: VRAM pressure estimate elevated; safe render-distance protection is active.
sodium-volt.notification.vram.critical: VRAM pressure estimate critical; reducing the safe render-distance cap.
sodium-volt.notification.vram.recovery: VRAM pressure estimate recovered; restoring one owned quality step.
sodium-volt.notification.apc.downshift: Volt APC reduced visual quality to stabilize %s FPS.
sodium-volt.notification.apc.recovery: Volt APC recovered one visual quality tier.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.enabled.too: Monitors a local session marker and can stage a conservative renderer safe mode after an unclean previous session or manual request. It cannot identify an exact crash cause, intercept normal Minecraft crash handling, or recover JVM/native failures that happen before Sodium Volt initializes. It never changes packs, shaders, graphics backend, mipmaps, servers, worlds, accounts, or sends telemetry.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.detect_uncl: Counts a bounded crash streak when the prior Sodium Volt session marker was not cleared by a clean client stop. This indicates an unclean previous session and only a possible renderer failure; it is not proof of a crash cause.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.automatic.t: Stages recovery after the detected unclean-session streak reaches the threshold and the attempt guard still permits it. Detection starts only after Sodium Volt Recovery initializes, so earlier JVM or native failures cannot be marked or recovered.
Requests one recovery attempt on the next launch even when automatic detection is disabled. The request is consumed only after recovery state, attempt count, and any required option backup are safely staged; the maximum-attempt guard still prevents loops.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.streak_thre: Sets how many detected unclean previous sessions are required before automatic safe mode. The marker cannot attribute an exact renderer or mod failure.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.maximum_att: Bounds persisted recovery attempts. At exhaustion Volt Recovery keeps monitoring and preserves any owned backup for clean restoration, but stops reapplying the profile, FPS cap, and APC suspension.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.safe_profil: Persists an ownership backup before reducing only proven-safe vanilla render settings. It never disables packs or shaders, switches graphics backend, changes mipmaps, or edits Sodium configuration files.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.render_dist: Caps render distance without ever raising a lower current value. VRAM Protection may lower it further, and ownership-aware restoration preserves any lower external, APC, or VRAM value.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.entity_dist: Caps vanilla entity render-distance scaling at this percentage without raising a lower value. Restoration changes it only while it still equals Volt Recovery's last applied value.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.reduce_grap: Applies a fast-style safe subset: clouds off, minimal particles, biome blend zero, entity shadows off, and ambient occlusion off. Minecraft's FAST preset is intentionally not invoked because it also changes mipmaps and unrelated options.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.limit_fps.t: Adds a transient recovery cap to the authoritative limiter. It composes by minimum with Minecraft, VSync, and Smart FPS and never rewrites or saves Max Framerate or VSync.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.fps_cap.too: Sets the transient maximum while recovery is active. A lower vanilla, VSync, or Smart FPS limit remains authoritative.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.suspend_apc: Resets and pauses Adaptive Performance Controller while recovery is active or an applied safe profile remains owned after stability. Turn this off to allow APC to adjust that profile. Volt Guard, VAPS, ATT, and performance-reducing VRAM protection may continue.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.restore_sta: Restore Owned Settings After Stable Session

After continuous valid rendered play reaches the stable duration, restores only fields still equal Volt Recovery's last applied values. If disabled, owned reduced graphics remain until runtime disable or clean stop. Player and external changes are preserved.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.stable_dura: Requires this many continuous seconds of valid, unpaused, in-world rendered frames before recovery is considered stable. Clock rollback safely restarts the timer.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.notificatio: Shows transition-only, rate-limited messages in a loaded world when no screen or overlay is open. Messages say possible renderer failure or manual recovery and never claim an exact crash cause.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.report.tool: Atomically replaces one bounded local fixed-schema report containing only reason, streak, attempt, profile state, and restoration result. It contains no paths, device or pack strings, server/world/account data, stack traces, telemetry, or network activity; Minecraft crash reports remain untouched.
sodium-volt.options.recovery.inspector_s: Show Recovery Stats in Volt Inspector
Shows a few bounded lines for monitoring, safe mode, loop guard, streak, attempt, owned profile, and stable countdown. No private strings or raw failure details are retained.
sodium-volt.notification.recovery.safe: Volt Recovery safe mode is active after a possible renderer failure.
sodium-volt.notification.recovery.manual: Volt Recovery safe mode is active by manual request.
sodium-volt.notification.recovery.stable: Volt Recovery reached a stable session and released transient protection.
sodium-volt.notification.recovery.loop_g: Volt Recovery attempt limit reached; automatic safe mode is paused.
sodium-volt.notification.recovery.watchd: Volt Recovery safe mode is active after a possible GPU/render stall.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.enabled.too: Runs one lazy, low-rate render-heartbeat monitor that can classify a long frame as a possible GPU/render stall. It cannot prove a GPU or driver hang, interrupt a blocked JVM/native call, replace the operating system's GPU timeout recovery, or guarantee a report before process termination. Disabled by default.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.warning_thr: Sets how long one eligible render frame must remain incomplete before a transition-only warning is recorded. Grace and suppression rules reset observations to reduce false positives.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.critical_th: Sets the earliest duration eligible for a confirmed critical incident. The effective value is always kept at least one second above the warning threshold; this remains only a possible GPU/render stall classification.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.confirmatio: Requires this many low-rate samples at or beyond the critical threshold in the same uninterrupted render frame before one incident is confirmed. Higher values reduce false positives but delay confirmation.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.startup_gra: Suppresses heartbeat classification after enabling the watchdog and whenever the loaded world identity changes. This avoids treating expected startup, join, leave, and dimension-transition work as a GPU/render stall.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.reload_grac: Suppresses monitoring during bounded tracked resource reloads and for this duration after each completion. Reload callbacks are generation-checked so stale completions cannot rearm a disabled or stopped watchdog.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.ignore_paus: Suppresses monitoring while paused, outside a fully loaded playable world, or while a screen or loading overlay is active. This is conservative and may intentionally ignore genuine stalls that occur only in those states.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.ignore_unfo: Suppresses monitoring while the game window is unfocused, minimized, or iconified, where operating-system scheduling and driver behavior can otherwise resemble a render stall.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.sample_inte: Sets the sleep interval of the single daemon monitor. Shorter intervals confirm closer to the threshold with slightly more wakeups; no per-sample logging, collections, UI access, or Minecraft/graphics API calls occur on that thread.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.cooldown.to: Requires this duration between confirmed incidents. A single stuck render frame is handled at most once, preventing report writes, Recovery staging, and notifications from retrying in a loop.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.maximum_inc: Bounds confirmed incident transitions for this game session. At the cap, heartbeat sampling remains bounded but no additional report or Recovery request is staged.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.arm_recover: After a confirmed possible GPU/render stall, atomically stages one small fixed-schema request for Volt Recovery on the next launch. Volt Recovery must be enabled, its persisted attempt guard remains authoritative, and the request is acknowledged only after Recovery durably stages an allowed activation.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.notificatio: Shows rate-limited warning or critical transition messages only after the render thread responds in a loaded world with no screen or overlay. It cannot display while the JVM or native render call remains blocked.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.report.tool: Atomically replaces one bounded local fixed-schema report containing only the possible-stall classification, bounded durations, thresholds, confirmation count, incident count, and whether Recovery staging succeeded. It stores no paths, device, driver, pack, server, world, account, stack, or telemetry data.
sodium-volt.options.watchdog.inspector_s: Show Watchdog Stats in Volt Inspector
Adds at most three bounded Inspector lines for current state, latest bounded duration, incident cap, and Recovery request status. It never exposes raw diagnostics or private strings.
sodium-volt.notification.watchdog.warnin: GPU Watchdog noticed a long render frame; no GPU or driver failure is proven.
sodium-volt.notification.watchdog.critic: GPU Watchdog confirmed a possible GPU/render stall; inspect the local bounded status.
sodium-volt.options.security.enabled.too: Preflights selected untrusted file and directory resource packs and applies live bounded stream guards before reload listeners consume their resources. It reduces path, archive expansion, image-size, JSON-depth, and core-shader override risks; it cannot prove a pack is trustworthy, inspect mod code, prevent every decoder or graphics-driver bug, or replace Minecraft and operating-system security. Java validation and vanilla file opening are not atomic: a concurrent local process with filesystem write access can swap a path between those operations. Static local and server-downloaded pack content remains covered by the stated bounds. Disabled by default.
sodium-volt.options.security.local_packs: Protects ordinary user and world resource packs identified exactly by Minecraft's DEFAULT or WORLD PackSource identity. Vanilla, built-in, feature, and custom mod resource sources are not wrapped. Local files remain on this device and are never hashed or transmitted.
sodium-volt.options.security.server_pack: Protects downloaded packs identified exactly by Minecraft's SERVER PackSource identity before reload work consumes them. It performs no network requests and stores no server, pack, resource, account, or world names.
sodium-volt.options.security.unsafe_path: Adds the configurable maximum path-length, path-depth, and strict lexical-name limits. Structural absolute, dot-segment, backslash, NUL, root-escape, symlink, dangling-symlink, and special-file checks remain baseline defenses when Shield and reject mode are enabled. Monitor-only mode observes these conditions but deliberately preserves vanilla behavior. Java check-to-open operations are not atomic against a concurrent local process that can mutate pack files.
sodium-volt.options.security.core_shader: Classifies files under assets/minecraft/shaders/core in monitored untrusted packs as policy violations. This reduces the risk from replacement core shaders but does not inspect shader semantics, mod-provided shader code, graphics drivers, or built-in resources.
sodium-volt.options.security.reject.tool: Fails the current resource reload through Minecraft's normal reload future when a policy violation is found. Turning this off uses monitor-only mode: violations are counted and optionally reported while vanilla pack behavior is preserved. Internal monitor failures are separately classified and keep the live bounded guards without permanently crashing the client.
sodium-volt.options.security.entry_limit: Bounds ZIP central entries, directory entries, overlay declarations, and live listed-resource outputs for each monitored pack. Lower values stop resource-count exhaustion sooner but may reject unusually large legitimate packs.
sodium-volt.options.security.archive_siz: Rejects a monitored ZIP whose on-disk regular-file size exceeds this limit before entry processing. This is distinct from expanded-size limits and does not extract or copy the archive.
sodium-volt.options.security.single_size: Bounds each declared uncompressed ZIP entry, each directory file, and each live returned resource stream. Reads stop in reject mode when changed content crosses the ceiling; monitor-only mode records the transition and preserves vanilla reads.
sodium-volt.options.security.total_budge: Bounds overflow-safe declared uncompressed bytes and the aggregate bytes returned by live resource streams for one opened monitored pack. Higher budgets accommodate larger packs but permit more resource work before protection acts.
sodium-volt.options.security.compression: Rejects entries whose declared uncompressed size is excessively large relative to compressed size, including non-empty zero-compressed-size claims. Unknown or ambiguous ZIP metadata is treated conservatively as a policy violation.
sodium-volt.options.security.png_dimensi: Reads only the bounded PNG signature and IHDR prefix and rejects zero, invalid, or oversized width or height before normal decoding. This cannot prevent every image-decoder, memory-allocation, or graphics-driver defect.
Applies an overflow-safe width-times-height ceiling from the PNG IHDR prefix. A lower area limit can protect earlier than the per-axis dimension limit but may reject very large panorama or high-resolution texture assets.
Lexically tracks object and array nesting with quote and escape handling for bounded .json and .mcmeta resources. It rejects mismatched, unterminated, or overly deep container structure but is not a semantic validator for every Minecraft JSON schema. Minecraft may read root pack.mcmeta once during repository discovery before the mapping-stable openFull protection boundary; Shield revalidates it before reload but cannot undo that earlier discovery read.
sodium-volt.options.security.path_length: Limits the number of characters in each monitored archive, directory, overlay, and live resource path when Strict Path Limits is enabled. Lower values reduce path-processing work but may reject packs with unusually long legitimate names.
Limits the number of slash-separated logical path components and filesystem path components when Strict Path Limits is enabled. Entry-count and scan-time settings separately bound traversal work; linked directories are not intentionally followed.
sodium-volt.options.security.scan_time.t: Caps preflight work across all monitored packs opened by one public resource reload, including nested reload tracking; each pack receives only the remaining time. A standalone pack open uses the same value as its per-open ceiling. Lower values reduce client-thread delay but can classify very large slow packs as timed out.
sodium-volt.options.security.notificatio: Shows only rate-limited rejected, monitored, or monitor-failure transitions after the tracked reload completes and a loaded-world UI state is safe. Messages contain no attacker-controlled names, paths, servers, worlds, accounts, or device strings.
sodium-volt.options.security.report.tool: Rate-limited atomic replacement writes one small exact-schema local report containing only fixed reason/source/action enums and bounded numeric counters. It stores no resource or pack names, paths, hashes, servers, worlds, accounts, devices, stack traces, telemetry, or network data.
sodium-volt.options.security.inspector_s: Show Shield Stats in Volt Inspector

Adds at most three bounded Inspector lines for mode, fixed source/reason categories, pack/resource counts, declared/read bytes, violations, rejections, and monitor failures. No attacker-controlled strings are retained or displayed.
sodium-volt.notification.resource_pack_s: Resource-Pack Shield rejected a monitored pack policy violation.
Resource-Pack Shield monitored a pack policy violation without rejecting it.
Resource-Pack Shield could not complete one preflight; live bounded guards remain active.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.enabled.tool: Intercepts an ordinary F2 screenshot, renders the next complete frame under a temporary privacy scope, and captures it before presentation. Only selected vanilla and Sodium Volt elements are suppressed; modded or third-party overlays cannot be guaranteed hidden, and shader or world pixels are not analyzed for private content. Graphics and HUD settings are never changed or saved. Debug panorama captures retain vanilla behavior. Disabled by default.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.hide_chat.to: Omits visible vanilla chat lines for the capture frame. Chat input is a separate Screen: it is refused while Block Capture with Screens Open is enabled, but this toggle does not sanitize it when screen blocking is turned off. It does not control chat overlays rendered independently by other mods.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.hide_debug.t: Omits the vanilla debug overlay for the capture frame, reducing exposure of coordinates, direction, performance, system, world, and server details. Debug information drawn by other mods is outside this guarantee.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.hide_player_: Omits the vanilla Tab player list for the capture frame so player names, skins, scores, and connection indicators are not extracted. Custom player lists rendered by mods may remain visible.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.hide_scorebo: Omits the vanilla scoreboard sidebar for the capture frame. This can conceal player, team, objective, and server-provided text, but cannot sanitize scoreboard-like overlays from other mods.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.hide_boss_ba: Omits vanilla boss bars and their labels for the capture frame. This avoids retaining server-provided boss text while leaving the underlying world scene untouched.
Omits vanilla title, subtitle-title, and action-bar messages for the capture frame. It does not clear or alter the messages and they can render normally on later frames.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.hide_subtitl: Skips vanilla sound-subtitle extraction for the capture frame. Subtitle state is not cleared, so accessibility information resumes on the following normal frame.
Omits vanilla toast notifications and the saving indicator for the capture frame without dismissing them. Toast-like UI rendered by a mod outside vanilla's toast manager may remain visible.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.hide_name_ta: Clears vanilla entity name-tag, score-text, and attachment render state only for entities extracted in the capture frame. It does not modify entity data and cannot guarantee removal of independently rendered modded labels.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.hide_gamepla: Optionally omits the vanilla crosshair, status effects, hotbar, health, armor, hunger, experience, air, mount, and related gameplay decorations for a cleaner screenshot. Sensitive text controls remain independent.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.hide_held_it: Optionally skips vanilla first-person hand and held-item submission for the capture frame. The inventory and equipped items are not changed; modded first-person renderers may not use this hook.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.block_screen: Refuses a privacy screenshot while a vanilla Screen or Overlay is open, including menus, chat screens, inventories, loading overlays, and pause UI. This is enabled by default because those surfaces cannot be reliably sanitized element by element.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.random_filen: Uses a bounded 128-bit cryptographically strong random token instead of Minecraft's local timestamp filename, with eight collision checks under the vanilla screenshots directory. The vanilla asynchronous PNG writer is retained and Sodium Volt adds no metadata. A separate local process with filesystem access can still race file operations.
Refuses the screenshot when a safe privacy capture cannot be prepared, or when a neutral filename cannot be prepared while Randomized Neutral Filename is enabled, instead of silently taking an unsanitized image. Turning this off permits vanilla fallback behavior where explicitly available and can expose content or a timestamp filename.
sodium-volt.options.privacy.notification: Shows fixed success, failure, blocked, or coalesced messages. Notifications never include the filename, absolute path, player, world, server, config values, or underlying exception details.
sodium-volt.notification.privacy.screen_: Privacy screenshot blocked while a screen or overlay is open.
sodium-volt.notification.privacy.unavail: Privacy screenshot is unavailable outside a loaded world.
sodium-volt.notification.privacy.coalesc: An additional privacy screenshot request was coalesced.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.enabled.too: Automatically distinguishes menus, integrated single-player saves, and multiplayer servers. The current global settings are captured before the first world profile is applied. Per-world and per-server records use bounded salted hashes; raw server addresses and world paths are never written to the Profiles config, shown in this UI, or logged.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.behavior.re: Restores only settings still owned by the departing profile when returning to a menu or disabling Profiles. Values changed afterward by you, Volt Recovery, APC, VRAM protection, or another mod are preserved and become the new global baseline.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.global.rend: Menu and fallback render-distance baseline. Larger distances make Sodium build, retain, and draw more chunk sections and can substantially increase CPU, GPU, and memory load. Performance impact: High.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.global.simu: Menu and fallback simulation-distance baseline. This mostly affects the integrated server; larger values keep more chunks ticking and can substantially increase CPU work. Performance impact: High.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.global.enti: Menu and fallback entity-distance scale. Higher percentages submit more distant entities and increase extraction and rendering work. Performance impact: Medium.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.global.fram: Menu and fallback FPS ceiling. A lower cap can reduce GPU load, power consumption, fan noise, and heat; Smart FPS and Recovery may impose a lower temporary effective limit. Performance impact: High.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.global.part: Menu and fallback vanilla particle density. Reduced modes decrease particle creation and rendering work but do not replace Volt Guard or VAPS budgets. Performance impact: Medium.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.single_play: Creates and reuses one bounded profile record for each integrated save. Distinct storage paths are salted and hashed before persistence, so saves with identical display names remain separate without retaining their paths.

Render distance used when a single-player save has no stored profile yet. Existing per-save records are unchanged until captured again. Larger values increase Sodium chunk preparation and rendering. Performance impact: High.
Integrated-server simulation distance used for a save's first profile. Larger values tick more chunks and can reduce client frame consistency on CPU-limited systems. Performance impact: High.
Entity-distance scale used for a save's first profile. Higher percentages keep more distant entities in rendering range. Performance impact: Medium.
FPS ceiling used for a save's first profile. Lower values reduce GPU demand and power use; other Volt controllers may temporarily lower it further. Performance impact: High.

Vanilla particle density used for a save's first profile. Reduced modes can improve busy-effect frame times while preserving critical-particle policy in other Volt features. Performance impact: Medium.

Captures the five current profile-owned settings into this integrated save's hashed record. Apply pending settings-screen changes first. This button does nothing outside an integrated single-player world. Performance impact: None until the profile is applied.

Removes only the current integrated save's hashed record. The active runtime settings are left untouched; the next visit creates a record from the Single Player template. Performance impact: None until the next visit.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.server.enab: Creates and reuses one bounded profile record for each multiplayer endpoint. The normalized endpoint is combined with a private random salt and SHA-256; raw addresses never enter the Profiles file, UI, or logs.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.server.rend: Render distance used when a server has no stored profile yet. Existing hashed server records are unchanged until captured again. Larger values increase Sodium chunk rendering and memory load. Performance impact: High.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.server.simu: Local simulation-distance preference stored for a server's first profile. Multiplayer servers may enforce their own view or simulation limits. Performance impact: High when locally effective.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.server.enti: Entity-distance scale used for a server's first profile. Lower values reduce distant entity extraction and rendering in crowded multiplayer scenes. Performance impact: Medium.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.server.fram: FPS ceiling used for a server's first profile. Lower limits reduce GPU pressure, power use, fan noise, and heat. Performance impact: High.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.server.part: Vanilla particle density used for a server's first profile. Reduced modes can help effect-heavy hubs and minigames without changing server behavior. Performance impact: Medium.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.server.capt: Captures the five current profile-owned settings into the current server's salted-hash record. Apply pending settings-screen changes first. No server address is retained or displayed. Performance impact: None until the profile is applied.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.server.forg: Removes only the current server's salted-hash record. Runtime settings remain untouched; the next visit creates a record from the Specific Server template. Performance impact: None until the next visit.
sodium-volt.options.profiles.factory_res: Opens a native Yes/No confirmation. Yes restores every Sodium Volt setting to its factory value, disables all feature master toggles, clears stored Profiles and transient ownership state, persists the result, and closes this settings screen so stale pending values cannot be reapplied. No makes no changes. Performance impact: Varies because every Volt feature is disabled.
